takeaway: Posterior duodenal ulcers, usually in the first part of the duodenum, erode into the gastroduodenal artery; anterior ulcers perforate into the peritoneal cavity.

lines.text: A 45-year-old man is bleeding from a duodenal ulcer.
lines.say: A forty-five-year-old man is bleeding from a duodenal ulcer.

lines.text: Duodenal ulcers commonly lie in the first, superior, part of the duodenum.
Ulcers that lie posteriorly erode into the gastroduodenal artery.
That is the source of this bleeding.
Ulcers that lie anteriorly erode into the peritoneal cavity instead, causing peritonitis.
Bleeding occurs in 20% of peptic ulcers, with a high mortality over the age of 55.
lines.say: Bleeding occurs in twenty percent of peptic ulcers, with a high mortality over the age of fifty-five.

lines.text: So the artery is the gastroduodenal artery.
